existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering
existing_roles.description:
Atomic Machines is building the Matter Compiler™, the first in a new class of AI-native, all-digital manufacturing systems that build working machines directly from code. The Matter Compiler (MC) is aimed at micro-machines: motors and gears the size of a grain of sand, robots small enough to work inside the body, cooling built directly into the chips that run AI, and the many devices like them that have been waiting on a way to build them. Its first product is PrimeSwitch™, an electromechanical power relay the size of a button battery that carries 150 amps continuous current and opens in 50 microseconds, about a thousand times faster than a conventional contactor. Founded by Jeff Holden — serial entrepreneur, ex-Amazon SVP and Uber's first Chief Product Officer — the company has raised $250 million to date.

Atomic Machines is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, with offices in Emeryville and Santa Clara.

### **About The Role:**

We are seeking a Senior Manager, Platform Manufacturing Engineering to lead Production Manufacturing Engineering as we scale the Matter Compiler from pilot production into high-volume manufacturing. You will own the equipment that builds our devices — its build, integration, bring-up, qualification and reliability — and the team of engineers who deliver it.

**You are an engineer first.** This is a player-coach role and the player half is not decorative: you will spearhead the hardest projects on the critical path personally, in CAD and on the floor, and use that work as the vehicle for coaching everyone around you. The fastest way to set a standard here is to define it while you produce work that meets it, then mentor your team to achieve the same bar.

Mentoring here happens inside the work, not alongside it. You will pull engineers onto the projects you lead, hand off scope as they are ready for it, review their designs with real technical depth, and grow the next set of project leads out of people who learned by building with you.

The management half is real. You will hire against a plan rather than a wish list, develop engineers toward the next level, run performance honestly, and install the operating standards this function works to — documentation, change control, qualification and release discipline, and what "done" means before work leaves the group. You will plan the organization ahead of where the business is today, own headcount and capital budget, and get manufacturability and equipment requirements into specifications set by other teams rather than reviewing them at the end.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Spearhead the hardest equipment projects on the critical path yourself — architecture, CAD, build, bring-up and qualification — and bring engineers along on them as the primary way they develop.
* Lead a team of 5–10 engineers spanning equipment design, automation and controls, integration, and sustaining, through a mix of direct reports and technical leads.
* Set the engineering standard by producing work to it: reference designs, qualification plans, RCCAs and documentation your team can pattern from, with the reasoning made explicit so it transfers.
* Coach through the work — pair on designs, run technical reviews with real depth, hand off scope as engineers are ready for it, and grow the next set of project leads out of people who built alongside you.
* Own the delivery record for the function — the equipment, qualifications and production readiness your team commits to, against committed dates.
* Lead equipment deployment end to end: installation, validation, commissioning, acceptance testing, SOP/WI release and operator qualification.
* Run root cause and corrective action personally on the failures that matter, teach the method by doing it in front of the team, and drive the corrective actions across teams that do not report to you.
* Install and uphold the operating standards: documentation, change control, qualification and release discipline, RCCA method and closure, and how work is reviewed before it leaves the group.
* Plan organizational growth — forecast hiring needs ahead of demand, define roles and levels, build and defend the hiring plan, and manage headcount and capital budget with Supply Chain and Finance.
* Own and resolve escalated personnel situations arising from business and priority changes, rather than routing them away.
* Get manufacturability and equipment requirements into specification setting and design milestones with Design Engineering and Product, rather than reviewing at the end.
* Balance competing priorities with peer leaders so committed deliverables are still met, and own communication of impact and resolution path where they cannot be.
* Own contract manufacturer and automation supplier execution through final integration and test to conformant hardware on schedule.
* Drive throughput, yield, cost and uptime improvement — held with control limits, not delivered as one-time gains — and establish the operating metrics and reporting cadence leadership can rely on without chasing.
* Travel between Emeryville and Santa Clara sites as needed.

### **What You'll Need:**

* 7+ years of manufacturing or equipment engineering experience, including 3+ years managing engineers with 5 or more direct reports.
* **Current hands-on capability.** You still design in CAD, still debug hardware on the floor, and could take the hardest open task on your team's board tomorrow. We will test this directly in the loop.
* Proven ownership of automated production equipment end to end — architecture through mechanical, controls and software integration, into a qualified, released system running in production.
* Proficiency in CAD for equipment design (SolidWorks, Onshape, AutoCAD or similar), with recent personal use.
* A track record of **developing engineers through the work** — specific people who grew because you put them on projects you were leading, reviewed their designs, and handed off scope as they were ready for it.
* A track record of building out a functional group: defining roles, hiring against a plan, and installing the operating standards — not only inheriting an existing team.
* Experience leading a team spanning more than one discipline (e.g., equipment, controls/automation, integration, sustaining), including people whose work sits outside your own background.
* Ownership of headcount and capital budget, with resourcing tradeoff decisions made under real constraint.
* Depth across DFx, RCCA, eBOMmBOM conversion, qualification and acceptance testing, and PLM/document control and release (Arena a plus).
* Experience in semiconductor, solar, hardware-based biotech, EV, or similar high-tech industries.
* Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functionally without authority — specifically, getting manufacturing and equipment requirements into specifications owned by other teams.
* A first-principles mindset — you question assumptions, reframe problems from the ground up, and approach challenges with a foundational understanding rather than relying solely on precedent.
* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

### **Bonus Points For:**

* Experience standing up or rebuilding a manufacturing or equipment engineering function at a company moving from pilot to production scale.
* Experience staying technically current while managing — a design, patent, or build you personally delivered while running a team.
* Knowledge of basic coding: RSLogix, Ignition, Python, or C/C++.

We are committed to an inclusive interview experience, including for individuals with disabilities. To request an accommodation, contact rc@atomicmachines.com. To help our recruiting team manage application volume and respond to candidates more efficiently, Atomic Machines may use AI-assisted tools.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Supply Chain (Robot Production)
existing_roles.description:
**About Genesis**
=================

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.

**The role**
============

Every part that goes into our robot: who makes it, at what price, on what lead time, to what quality. This is the hands-on role. You build the supplier base for production, develop domestic sources for the sub-systems that need them, and make sure the line never waits on a part. You start with a bill of materials, a design team and a few suppliers; you end with a qualified, dual-sourced supply chain that supports production with our manufacturing partner. You are at our facility, at the partner and at suppliers more than you are at a desk.

**What you'll do**
==================

* Be on the floor: at our facility, at our manufacturing partner and at suppliers; first articles, line-down calls and recoveries are yours.
* Build the supplier base: source, qualify and manage suppliers for machined and cast structures, gears and actuators, motors, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two sources for every critical sub-system.
* Develop domestic suppliers for the sub-systems that need them, and keep the content records that come with selling into regulated markets.
* Run the commercial work day to day: RFQs, should-cost, piece price and tooling negotiation, payment and warranty terms; work with Legal on supplier agreements.
* Sit in design reviews from the start: flag long-lead, single-source and high-risk parts before design freeze; bring supplier capability into the design.
* Own clear-to-build and the plan: every unit on the schedule has a complete kit before it starts; a rolling plan the line, the partner and the suppliers all see; capacity planning with suppliers ahead of demand; inventory accuracy and safety stock by part class.
* Own the BOM in production: cost roll-ups by phase, engineering change control with the design team and Manufacturing Engineering, cost-down from pilot to volume.
* Build the supplier quality loop with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality: first article and PPAP where it applies, incoming inspection, supplier scorecards and quarterly reviews, corrective action and recovery.
* Run logistics: inbound, between our facility and our partner's, import and export paperwork with Legal, spares and service parts.
* Run the systems we have and help stand up the next ones: part numbering, BOM control, MRP; own the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, PPV, inventory).

**What we are looking for**
===========================

* You have built a supplier base for a hardware product going into production, not managed or handed to you, and you produce results in weeks, not quarters.
* Deep experience with machined and cast metal parts, gears or actuators, motors, PCBAs and harnesses, and the suppliers who make them; you read drawings and GD&T.
* You have developed new suppliers in new regions and qualified them to a standard.
* Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers.
* You are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and cost roll-ups, and comfortable with the people who design the product.
* 8 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or supplier development for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what the systems look like at scale; you have led a small team or are ready to; engineering degree preferred.
* Bonus: robotics or automotive; contract manufacturer selection and transition; import and export compliance; APICS or CPSM.

**Working Conditions**
======================

Office and production environments; travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 30%.

**How we work**
===============

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

* **Limitless ambition.** We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
* **Relentless urgency.** Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
* **Type-2 Fun.** Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
* **Radical transparency.** Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
* **Multiculturalism**. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
* **Team over ego.** Help others, share context, and win as a team.
* **A joyful journey.** We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

----------------

**A Day In The Life**
---------------------

Every day at Hubbell is different and you’ll contribute in many ways. On any given day, you’ll make a difference by:

Serving in a leadership role, directly supervising project engineers and designers.

Overseeing, managing, and supporting calibration programs for the facilities, including production equipment, facility equipment.

Developing concepts for new and revised products maximizing function, safety, features, and user benefits while minimizing costs.

Directing preparation of models and lab testing as required to develop product.

Preparing and maintaining Project Control Charts and schedules.

Participating in meetings as required to communicate and coordinate projects with various departments within Hubbell.

Developing the site maintenance budget for approval and managing site budget costs to meet the approved budget targets.

Directing preparation of product drawings and checking completed drawings.

Preparing product standards and specifications and obtaining agency listings as required (UL/CSA etc.).

Approving tooling, assemblies, and updating drawings. Release approved product for production.

**What will help you thrive in this role?**
-------------------------------------------

Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (required)

10+ years of relevant experience (required)

5+ supervisory experience in an engineering related field (required)

Ability to check design drawings with extreme thoroughness while paying strict attention to detail

Ability to manage multiple design projects with varying priority levels

Proven track record working with systems engineering functions including concept of operations development, requirements management, technical risk management, interface definition and control

Experience effectively communicating and presenting with all levels of management and individual contributors on the program team

Strong organization, coordination, planning and collaboration skills

Experience supporting engineering teams in a multi-discipline environment

Experience conducting system integration and system tests to include development of integration and test plans, test cases and procedures

Ability to visualize system functionality, to create block diagrams, and to analyze system performance

Hubbell creates critical infrastructure solutions that power our customers, communities, people and the planet. Our company is strategically aligned around enabling grid modernization and electrification. As more products plug in to an aging grid, Hubbell solutions enable the transition to a more reliable, resilient and efficient energy infrastructure. Founded in 1888 our innovation has made us a leading global manufacturer of high quality electrical and utility solutions enabling customers to operate critical infrastructure reliably and efficiently.

The company operates in two segments. Hubbell Utility Solutions (HUS) enable the grid to conduct, communicate and control energy across utility applications and Hubbell Electrical Solutions (HES) are essential to managing power across a wide range of industries and applications. Our vertical market solutions can be applied to markets including Data Centers, Renewables, Commercial Buildings, Industrial, Telecom and Transportation. Supporting both of our business segments is our corporate and Hubbell Unified Business Solutions teams that provide consistent process, tools technologies across our businesses.

We are committed to operating sustainably and ethically while promoting an inclusive and supportive culture for our people to grow and develop in their careers. Our employees proudly work and serve our communities from our headquarters in Shelton, CT, across the United States and around the globe.

Hubbell Utility Solutions (HUS) enable the grid to conduct, communicate and control energy across utility applications. HUS provides the critical components that allow the grid to reliably transmit and distribute energy, as well as the communications and controls technologies to make the grid smarter and more flexible.

**Job Title:**

**Senior Plant Manager** (Corona, CA)

**Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World**

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with 96,000 other curious, creative 3Mers.

**This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military environments to a 3M career.**

**The Impact You’ll Make in this Role** 
As the **Senior Plant Manager,** you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

 

* Active and visible EHS ownership to ensure site compliance, stewardship and championing continuous improvement efforts to improve all aspects of EHS.

* Managing supply chain execution and inventory management to ensure appropriate supply chain performance through responsiveness, delivery performance, capacity management, supplier management, and appropriate inventory management.
* Represent 3M and engage with key accounts.

* Bachelor's degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start)

* Five (5) years of manufacturing experience in a private, public, government or military environment

* Certified LSS BB or MBB
* Experience in Operations Management

**SENIOR MANAGER, QUALITY IMPROVEMENT**

**What you’ll do.**

As the Senior Manager, Quality Improvement, you’ll help neurologists put evidence into practice by managing the processes that support clinical practice guidelines, evidence-based publications, and resources. You’ll advance the AAN’s strategic objectives by supporting the development of timely, evidence-based clinical guidelines, editorial and dissemination strategies, and meaningful resources that engage neurologists in improving their practice. Working across divisions, you’ll connect clinical practice and quality efforts to deliver value for AAN members.

**Please review the attached job description for full details. If viewing from an external site, please visit** **https://www.aan.com/about-the-aan/work-at-the-aan****.**

**Who we are.**

Join a diverse community of fun, energetic, and dedicated employees and members who are committed to supporting neurologists worldwide in providing exceptional care to their patients. The AAN's vision is to be indispensable to our members, and we continue to embrace our values of Community, Leadership, Well-being and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. Together, we pursue our mission to enhance member career fulfillment and promote brain health for all.

The AAN, founded in Minneapolis in 1948, supports and represents more than 44,000 neurologists and neuroscience professionals worldwide who provide crucial patient care, seek new cures and treatments for brain disease and work to ensure patient access to the right care. Our headquarters is in a stunning, energy-efficient office, located in downtown Minneapolis’s dynamic Mill District, and our public policy office is near the action on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC. Both locations offer easy access to light rail, major bus lines, parking options, walking/biking paths, and a myriad of dining and entertainment choices, making it a vibrant hub for everyone.

**What we look for.**

**Education:**

* Bachelor's degree in Public Health, Health Care Management, Health Sciences, Nursing, or related field

**Experience:**

* Minimum of 5 years of related experience in healthcare management and quality improvement
* Minimum of 3 years of supervisory experience
* Minimum of 3 years of project management experience
* Demonstrated ability to uphold the AAN’s values
* Demonstrated ability to supervise a team in a fast-paced environment and nurture individual career development and growth
* Ability to provide clear instructions and successful presentations to staff, work groups and panels
* Demonstrated skill, tact, diplomacy, confidentiality, and professionalism in interactions with teams, members, and other relevant individuals or groups
* Demonstrated proficiency using MS Office for word, spreadsheet, and presentations
* Excellent time management skills, ability to deliver results when facing multiple projects with tight deadlines
* Advanced knowledge of evidence-based medicine and clinical practice guideline development is preferred
* Knowledge of established evidence grading, and recommendation-development methods, such as GRADE or comparable frameworks is preferred
* Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and physician or subject-matter expert panels through complex evidence-based projects is preferred
* Demonstrated experience providing strategic and operational leadership for multiple concurrent, multi-year programs or projects is preferred
* Experience identifying and implementing process improvements, technology, or emerging approaches is preferred

*Relevant education and/or experience exceeding the required qualifications may be substituted on a year-for-year basis.*

**Travel Requirements:** Minimal travel required – up to 5%

**Location:** Minneapolis, MN and is identified as hybrid (required to work in the office with the ability to work remotely part of the week)

**Schedule:** Occasional evening and weekends required

**What we offer.**

Our excellent benefits package that works as hard for you as you do for us.

* **Thrive at Work and Beyond**
 + Flexible work arrangements
 + Generous PTO & holidays
 + Comprehensive wellness programs
 + Paid parental, family, and bereavement leave
* **Benefits to Secure Your Future**
 + Competitive salary & incentive program
 + 10.5% 401(k) contribution & financial planning resources
 + Paid life, and both long- and short-term disability insurance
* **Benefits to Grow With Us**
 + Tuition reimbursement
 + Professional development opportunities
 + Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion training programs

 + Employee awards & peer recognition to celebrate excellence

 + Diversity, Equity & Inclusion initiatives to create a culture where everyone belongs
 + Volunteer days & charitable giving programs to make an impact beyond the workplace
* **Health & Happiness (Medical, Dental, Vision & More)**

 + Telemedicine & mental health resources for accessible care
 + Onsite workout facility, gender-neutral restroom, wellness and lactation rooms
 + Transportation subsidy

Our headquarters is in a stunning, energy-efficient office, located in downtown Minneapolis’s dynamic Mill District, and our public policy office is near the action on Capitol Hill in Washington, DC. Both locations offer easy access to light rail, major bus lines, parking options, walking/biking paths, and a myriad of dining and entertainment choices, making it a vibrant hub for everyone.

**Great People in Great Careers:** The AAN offers talent opportunities in the fields of Administration, Accounting, Marketing, Communications, Digital Development, Event Planning, Social Media, Research, Health Policy, Information Systems, Project Management, and more.

**ADDITIONAL RESOURCES**

View our press room, conferences, world-renowned guidelines, social media channels, patient and caregiver magazine, and most recent Annual Report.

existing_roles.title: Senior Director, Quality Control
existing_roles.description:
Crescent Biopharma’s vision is to build a world leading oncology company bringing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients. The Company’s clinical-stage pipeline includes its lead program, a PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody, as well as novel antibody-drug conjugates. By leveraging multiple modalities and established targets, Crescent aims to rapidly advance potentially transformative therapies as single agents and as part of combination regimens to treat a range of solid tumors. For more information, visit www.crescentbiopharma.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn and X.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Director, Quality Control to join as a key leader within Crescent's Quality organization, responsible for providing strategic and hands-on Quality Control leadership across company’s biologics and ADC programs, and future pipeline growth. Partnering closely with Analytical Sciences, GMP Quality Assurance, CMC/Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs, you will provide phase-appropriate QC oversight from early development through late-stage development and commercialization within a global outsourced testing and manufacturing network. You will ensure reliable release and stability testing while building the QC infrastructure, laboratory network, and operating controls needed to advance programs into Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA submission, and commercial readiness.

Crescent's operating model requires clear, collaborative accountability between Analytical Sciences and QC. Analytical Sciences leads analytical development and performs the primary technical work through method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and PPQ readiness. QC provides oversight and operational input during early development, assumes increasing responsibility for method transfer, validation execution oversight, laboratory readiness, and GMP testing as programs mature, and takes primary ownership of routine QC operations and analytical method lifecycle management following transition to late-stage and commercial operations.

Success in this role requires a collaborative, hands-on leader who understands both analytical development and commercial QC operations, can establish effective governance across internal and external partners, and thrives in a fast-paced biotechnology environment while balancing scientific rigor, compliance, speed, and pragmatism.

### **Responsibilities**

* Define and implement Crescent's phase-appropriate QC strategy and operating model across early development, Phase 3, PPQ, regulatory submission, and commercialization, with clear decision rights and handoffs among Analytical Sciences, QC, and GMP QA.
* Oversee QC activities for drug substance, drug product, intermediates, finished goods, in-process, release, characterization, and stability testing across the portfolio.
* Provide QC oversight and operational requirements during early development while Analytical Sciences leads method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and method maturation through PPQ readiness.
* Partner with Analytical Sciences on integrated Phase 3 and PPQ readiness, including method validation and transfer, laboratory qualification, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, stability, sample management, and testing timelines.
* Lead QC execution oversight for method transfer, validation, and laboratory readiness; following transition to GMP QC operations, own routine method lifecycle management, performance monitoring, changes, revalidation, transfers, and remediation.
* Lead outsourced GMP QC operations, including sample management and testing coordination, and ensure timely, compliant release and stability testing for clinical supply, PPQ, batch disposition, regulatory commitments, and future commercial supply.
* Partner with Analytical Sciences, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, and QA on specifications and stability strategy; lead operational implementation, stability execution, data review, trending, and escalation within the QC network.
* Establish and oversee reference standard and critical reagent programs, including qualification, bridging, inventory, monitoring, replacement, and lifecycle planning.
* Provide technical leadership for OOS, OOT, OOE, atypical results, invalid assays, laboratory deviations, CAPAs, and change controls, ensuring scientifically sound, timely investigations and risk-based escalation.
* Lead selection, onboarding, qualification, governance, and performance management of CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including agreements, capacity, metrics, issue management, data integrity, and inspection readiness.
* Provide QC input to CMC and regulatory strategies and support IND/IMPD, BLA/MAA, health authority, and inspection activities; ensure commitments are implemented within the laboratory network.
* Lead alliance management with business partners on QC matters, including governance, roles and responsibilities, shared testing and release requirements, issue escalation, decision-making, and alignment on development, regulatory, and future commercial priorities.
* Establish scalable QC procedures, systems, metrics, budgeting, forecasting, and resource plans; support compliant use of LIMS, stability, analytical data, and trending tools, and build internal QC capability as Crescent advances toward commercialization.
* Mentor staff and consultants and foster a culture of scientific rigor, collaboration, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement while staying current with evolving GMP, ICH, compendial, and industry expectations.

### **Education & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in life sciences, analytical sciences, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum 10-12 years of progressive experience in biologics QC, analytical development, or related CMC functions, including leadership of GMP QC operations in an outsourced environment.
* Experience with biologics analytical methods, including cell-based bioassays/potency assays; ADC and other complex biologic modality experience is preferred.
* Experience supporting biologics from clinical development through Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA, and commercial readiness; bispecific antibody, ADC, or other complex modality experience is a plus.
* Proven experience transitioning methods from development into routine GMP QC use, including qualification, validation, transfer, implementation, performance monitoring, and lifecycle management.
* Strong experience with release and stability testing, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, OOS/OOT/OOE investigations, analytical trending, deviations, CAPAs, and change control.
* Demonstrated success overseeing CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including qualification, governance, investigations, capacity, performance, and issue resolution.
* Strong knowledge of global GMP regulations, FDA/EMA/ICH guidance, compendial expectations, data integrity, Part 11 / Annex 11, and phase-appropriate application across development and commercial operations.
* Experience supporting regulatory submissions, health authority questions, pre-approval inspections, and commercial inspection readiness.
* Ability to establish clear roles and effective collaboration among Analytical Sciences, QC, GMP QA, CMC/Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and external partners.
* Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach, solutions-oriented leader who communicates clearly, applies pragmatic science- and risk-based judgment, works effectively in a fast-paced small-company environment, and can travel to external sites as needed.
* Commitment to living Crescent’s core values and operating norms.

### **What We Offer**

* Opportunity to join a mission-driven team where you'll contribute to impactful work, take on varied responsibilities, and grow quickly in a dynamic environment
* Competitive compensation, including base salary, performance bonus, and equity
* 100% employer-paid benefits package
* Flexible PTO
* Two, one-week company-wide shutdowns each year
* A commitment to your professional development, with access to resources, mentorship, and growth opportunities

### **Salary Range**

The salary range for this position is $260,000 to $285,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but is not limited to relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography.

**Additional Description for Pay Transparency:**

The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but is not limited to relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography. Subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees and/or eligible dependents are eligible to participate in the following Company sponsored employee benefit programs: medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short- and long-term disability. Subject to the terms of their respective plans, employees are eligible to participate in the Company’s savings plan (401(k)). This position is eligible to participate in the Company’s long-term incentive program. Subject to the terms of their respective policies and date of hire, Employees are eligible for the following time off benefits: Vacation – Unlimited PTO; Sick time – 10 days per calendar year; Holiday pay, including two Company shut downs; Parental Leave – 16 weeks within one year of the birth/adoption/foster care of a child; FMLA; Military Leave. Additional information can be found - https://www.crescentbiopharma.com/careers/#benefits

Please note:

Crescent Biopharma is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status.

**Please note, Crescent does not accept unsolicited resumes from external agencies or recruiters. Submission of a resume without a prior written agreement does not create any express or implied contract between Crescent and the agency. Crescent will not pay any fees related to unsolicited resumes.**

existing_roles.description:
**Since 1869, we've connected people through food they love. We’re proud to be stewards of amazing brands that people trust. Our portfolio includes the iconic Campbell’s brand, as well as Cape Cod, Chunky, Goldfish, Kettle Brand, Lance, Late July, Pacific Foods, Pepperidge Farm, Prego, Pace, Rao’s Homemade, Snack Factory, Snyder’s of Hanover. Swanson, and V8.**

**Here, you will make a difference every day. You will be supported to build a rewarding career with opportunities to grow, innovate and inspire. Make history with us.**

**Why Campbell’s…**

* Benefits begin on day one and include medical, dental, short and long-term disability, AD&D, and life insurance (for individual, families, and domestic partners).
* Employees are eligible for our matching 401(k) plan and can enroll on the first day of employment with immediate vesting.
* Campbell’s offers unlimited sick time along with paid time off and holiday pay.
* If in WHQ – free access to the fitness center. Access to on-site day care (operated by Bright Horizons) and company store.
* Giving back to the communities where our employees work and live is very important to Campbell’s. Our “Campbell’s Cares” program matches employee donations and/or volunteer activity up to $1,500 annually.
* Campbell’s has a variety of Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) to support employees.

**Sr. Director, Supply Quality and Warehouse and Distribution Quality**

The Sr. Director, Supply Quality and Warehouse and Distribution Quality is responsible for leading a comprehensive supply quality, warehouse quality, and distribution quality program across ingredients, packaging, suppliers, warehouses, distributors, and external partners. This role partners closely with Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, R&D, Regulatory, Legal, plant operations, warehouse and distribution teams, suppliers, brokers, distributors, customers, and third parties to drive quality, compliance, supply continuity, and execution excellence. The director establishes and executes strategy, strengthens governance and systems, leverages data and digital tools to proactively manage risk, serves as a key customer interface, and owns critical customer quality relationships to build trust, resolve issues, and deliver on customer, consumer, brand, and business expectations.

 

**What you will do…**

* Strategic Leadership: Define, communicate, and execute the supply quality and warehouse and distribution quality strategy, roadmap, objectives, and programs across the supply network. Lead with a systems-thinking approach to prioritize risk, align resources, and drive measurable results.
* Category and Network Oversight: Provide leadership across ingredient, packaging, supplier, warehouse, and distributor categories, applying deep quality expertise to materials, storage, handling, processes, and network performance.
* Standards and Systems Management: Establish, interpret, communicate, and strengthen policies, standards, procedures, specifications, verification, and validation processes to ensure consistent execution of warehouse, distribution, regulatory, and quality expectations.
* Risk and Compliance Leadership: Identify, assess, and mitigate quality, regulatory, operational, and reputational risks across the supply base, warehouse network, and distribution network. Oversee risk assessments, ratings, audits, compliance, nonconformances, and business continuity actions.
* Audit and Verification Oversight: Lead audit strategy and governance, including planning, auditor capability development, execution oversight, corrective action follow-up, and continuous improvement of supplier, warehouse, and distributor verification programs.
* Performance Management and Analytics: Lead the use of metrics, data analytics, digital tools, and AI-enabled insights to monitor supplier, warehouse, and distributor performance, identify trends, accelerate decision-making, and improve accountability, transparency, and consistency.
* Supplier, Warehouse, and Distributor Performance: Oversee relationship management, improvement initiatives, contract and performance reviews, and resource deployment to improve quality, compliance, and service outcomes across the network.
* Regulatory and Industry Leadership: Apply deep knowledge of applicable regulations and industry expectations to guide program design, ensure compliance, and influence best-in-class execution across the supply, warehouse, and distribution network.
* Customer Interface and Relationship Ownership: Serve as a key customer interface for quality-related matters and own strategic customer relationships. Build credibility and trust, lead quality discussions, respond to customer concerns, align on expectations, and drive effective resolution of quality, compliance, and service issues.
* Cross-Functional and Enterprise Collaboration: Partner across supply chain, quality, regulatory, legal, R&D, operations, and external stakeholders to align priorities, influence change, and deliver integrated solutions that protect the business and strengthen performance.
* People and Resource Leadership: Lead, coach, and develop talent while overseeing internal, supplier, and third-party resources. Build a high-performing team environment focused on accountability, capability building, and continuous improvement.
Benchmarking and Continuous Improvement: Benchmark internal and external best practices, incorporate learnings into systems and processes, and drive future-ready capabilities across supply quality and warehouse and distribution quality. 

 

**Who you will work with…**

Collaborate closely with Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain, R&D, Legal, Regulatory, plant operations, warehouse and distribution teams, suppliers, distributors, brokers, customers, and third-party partners.

 

**What you bring to the table… (Must Have)**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree in a relevant field preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality, supply quality, warehouse quality, or distribution quality management experience in food manufacturing, consumer products, logistics, or a related industry.

existing_roles.description:
This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for a proven manufacturing executive with deep **paper manufacturing and paper machine operations experience**. Our client is seeking a hands-on, results-driven leader who can take full ownership of plant performance, strengthen operational discipline, and lead the facility to improved results across **safety, quality, production, reliability, cost and people development**.

The successful candidate will be responsible for all aspects of plant operations and will play a key role in driving performance improvements, stabilizing underperforming areas, and building a strong culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

This role is ideal for a seasoned Plant Manager or senior operations leader who understands the complexity of paper manufacturing and has a track record of improving plant performance through strong leadership, technical knowledge, disciplined execution and data-driven decision-making.

The Plant Manager will oversee the day-to-day and strategic leadership of the facility, ensuring the plant operates safely, efficiently and profitably while developing both leadership and frontline teams.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead all plant operations to achieve established **safety, quality, production, reliability and financial objectives**.
* Build and reinforce a strong **safety culture** through visible leadership, clear expectations, coaching and accountability at all levels of the organization.
* Oversee plant performance and ensure operations are aligned with productivity, quality and cost targets.
* Optimize **paper machine performance**, equipment uptime, production output and finished-product quality.
* Improve equipment reliability through strong maintenance systems, including preventive and predictive maintenance, planning and scheduling, and root cause analysis.
* Manage and improve plant financial performance, including cost-per-ton, labour, maintenance, fibre, chemical and energy costs.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts using structured, data-driven problem-solving methodologies to improve operational and financial results.
* Develop and execute recovery or turnaround plans for underperforming operations, establishing clear priorities, ownership, milestones and measurable outcomes.
* Build, coach and strengthen plant leadership, technical and hourly teams through employee development, performance management, succession planning and accountability.
* Partner with maintenance, production, quality and leadership teams to ensure cross-functional alignment and effective execution of plant priorities.
* Establish a culture focused on **performance, engagement, ownership and continuous improvement**.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a strong plant leader with deep technical and operational knowledge of **paper manufacturing**, particularly **paper machine operations**, who can lead a large team and drive measurable business results.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in **Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing** or a related field is preferred.
* 10–15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* **Must have direct paper manufacturing experience**, including demonstrated technical knowledge of **paper machine operations**.
* Proven experience leading paper machine operations and delivering sustainable improvements in performance, reliability and quality.
* Demonstrated success improving underperforming facilities or leading plant turnaround/recovery initiatives.
* Strong understanding of **papermaking processes, maintenance and reliability systems, plant operations and financial management**.
* Experience managing key manufacturing metrics, including productivity, equipment uptime, cost control and quality performance.
* Proven ability to lead large teams, develop talent, drive accountability and guide organizational change effectively.
* Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence performance at all levels of the plant.

Pay: $150,000.00 - $180,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Relocation assistance
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Enter your email
* Available time for call

Experience:

* tissue and paper manufacturing operation: 10 years (Required)

Work Location: On the road

We are searching for a seasoned manufacturing executive to oversee our facility, focusing on operational success and high-level performance. As the **Plant Manager**, you will hold total accountability for the site, encompassing safety protocols, product quality, logistical delivery, cost management, infrastructure investment, and the facility's overall financial health.

You will function as the primary operational authority at the site, reporting to the President, while providing leadership to the Engineering, Quality, Production, Materials, and Maintenance departments.

**Core Accountabilities**

* Foster a workplace culture centered on accountability, safety, and ongoing operational refinement.
* Ensure the site meets its targets for financial health, on-time shipping, inventory accuracy, and labor output.
* Oversee the facility's capital investments, operational spending, and departmental budgets.
* Mentor and cultivate the growth of cross-functional teams and management staff.
* Implement process enhancements to boost efficiency, minimize waste, and elevate the customer experience.
* Collaborate with senior executives to implement long-term growth strategies.
* Leverage manufacturing software and ERP tools to track performance metrics and hit operational targets.

**Required Qualifications**

* Over a decade of manufacturing background, with at least five years in a Plant Manager or Director of Operations capacity holding full site responsibility.
* Demonstrated history of successfully overseeing a manufacturing plant of similar or greater scale.

* Proven track record of managing capital improvement projects that yield significant operational gains.
* Background in managing diverse functions including Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, Production, and Materials.

**Preferred Background**

* History of overseeing operations across multiple locations.

* Fluency in both Spanish and English.

* Monitoring of KPIs and operational metrics.

existing_roles.description:
Description:

**Plant Manager** 
**Location:** United Rolls Inc. In Canton, Ohio 
**Department:** Operations 
**Reports To:** President 
**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Position Summary**

The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, performance, safety, quality, and profitability of United Rolls Inc.'s manufacturing operations, including an iron foundry and machine shop specializing in the production of centrifugal spun cast iron rolls for the steel, aluminum, paper, plastics, and other industrial processing industries. This position directs all aspects of production, maintenance, quality assurance, engineering, environmental compliance, and workforce development to ensure on-time delivery of world-class products while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and operational excellence.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Safety and Environmental Leadership**

* Establish and maintain a strong safety culture throughout the foundry and machine shop operations.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, state environmental regulations, and company safety policies.
* Lead incident investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
* Conduct regular safety audits, risk assessments, and safety training programs.
* Drive continuous improvement in safety metrics, including reduction of recordable incidents and near misses.

**Operations Management**

* Direct daily operations of the iron foundry, centrifugal casting processes, heat treatment operations, roll finishing, and machine shop activities.
* Ensure production schedules meet customer delivery requirements while maintaining efficiency and quality standards.
* Monitor plant productivity, capacity utilization, scrap rates, and operational performance metrics.
* Coordinate production planning, workflow optimization, and resource allocation.
* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Foundry Management**

* Oversee all foundry operations including:
* Melting and pouring of iron alloys.
* Centrifugal casting of rolls.
* Mold preparation and handling.
* Heat treatment processes.
* Metallurgical testing and quality control.
* Ensure proper process controls are maintained to achieve customer specifications and metallurgical requirements.
* Drive improvements in yield, casting quality, and process consistency.

**Machine Shop Leadership**

* Manage machining operations involving large CNC and manual equipment used in roll finishing.
* Optimize machine utilization, tooling performance, setup reduction, and throughput.
* Ensure proper maintenance and calibration of machine tools and inspection equipment.
* Support implementation of advanced machining technologies and automation where appropriate.

**Quality Assurance**

* Partner with Quality and Metallurgical teams to ensure product integrity.
* Lead efforts to reduce defects, rework, customer complaints, and warranty claims.
* Ensure compliance with ISO and customer quality standards.
* Review and analyze quality metrics and implement corrective actions.

**Maintenance and Reliability**

* Direct preventive and predictive maintenance programs for foundry and machining equipment.
* Develop capital improvement and equipment replacement plans.
* Minimize downtime through effective maintenance planning and reliability strategies.
* Oversee utilities, plant infrastructure, and critical support systems.

**Financial Management**

* Develop and manage annual operating budgets.
* Monitor labor, material, energy, maintenance, and overhead costs.
* Identify and implement cost reduction initiatives.
* Analyze production and operational data to maximize profitability.
* Support capital investment planning and ROI analysis.

**Leadership and Workforce Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop supervisors, managers, and hourly employees.
* Foster employee engagement, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Support workforce planning, succession planning, and talent development efforts.
* Collaborate with Human Resources on hiring, performance management, and employee relations.
* Maintain positive labor-management relationships where applicable.

**Customer and Business Support**

* Support sales and customer service teams by ensuring manufacturing capabilities align with customer requirements.
* Participate in customer visits, audits, and technical reviews.
* Work closely with engineering on new product development and process improvements.
* Maintain strong communication with suppliers and contractors.

**Position Impact**

The Plant Manager plays a critical leadership role in ensuring United Rolls Inc. delivers high-quality spun cast iron rolls safely, efficiently, and profitably while driving continuous improvement and supporting the company's long-term growth objectives.

Requirements:

**Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Metallurgy, Industrial Management, or related field preferred.
* Equivalent combination of education and industry experience may be considered.

**Experience**

* Minimum 10 years of manufacturing leadership experience.
* Minimum 5 years in a plant management, operations management, or senior production leadership role.
* Strong experience in foundry operations, metal casting, steel or iron manufacturing, heavy industrial manufacturing, or related industries.
* Experience managing machining operations and large CNC equipment preferred.
* Proven success leading safety, quality, productivity, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**Technical Knowledge**

* Iron metallurgy and centrifugal casting processes.
* Foundry operations and heat treatment processes.
* CNC machining and machining best practices.
* Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Quality management systems and root cause analysis.
* Maintenance and reliability management.
* ERP/MRP manufacturing systems.
* OSHA and environmental compliance standards.

**Required Competencies**

* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Strategic thinking and business acumen.
* Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
* Results-oriented with a continuous improvement mindset.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* High level of accountability and integrity.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

* OSHA Recordable Incident Rate
* Lost Time Accident Rate
* On-Time Delivery Performance
* Production Throughput
* Scrap and Yield Performance
* Cost Per Ton Produced
* Machine Utilization
* Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE)
* Customer Quality Performance
* Employee Retention and Engagement
* Maintenance Downtime
* EBITDA/Operating Profit Contribution

**Physical and Work Environment Requirements**

* Frequent presence in foundry and machine shop environments.
* Exposure to heat, noise, dust, moving equipment, and industrial hazards.
* Ability to walk production areas daily and occasionally climb stairs, ladders, and platforms.
* Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).

The estimated base salary range for this role is $200,000 to $235,000 per year, plus an annual incentive bonus and equity. 
Individual pay is based upon location, skills and expertise, experience and other relevant factors

**What does it mean to work at Arktura LLC, a subsidiary of Armstrong World Industries?**

It means being immersed in a supportive culture that recognizes you as a key player in Armstrong's future. We are a large company with a local feel, where you will get to know and collaborate with leadership and your colleagues across the company. Arktura LLC is a widely published company headquartered in a fast-paced design office and manufacturing facility in Los Angeles, CA. We design, develop, and manufacture a variety of façade systems, interior wall and ceiling systems, custom art installations on a full range of state-of-the-art equipment, in our 100,000 sf facility.

Working at Arktura is the best! Benefits include 401k with employee match, robust health care options, paid time off and professional development. We have a casual dress code, free snacks, and quarterly events! As a company, we love to engage in community service activities with our local organizations. We provide access to 100’s of discounts, specialty savings and voluntary benefits through LifeMart such as car and hotel rentals and auto, home, and pet insurance, legal services, and childcare We support Employee Resource Groups created to connect employees with common interests to promote inclusion and provide perspective.

 

We’re looking for an experienced Plant Manager to lead Arktura’s manufacturing operations in Carson, California. This is an opportunity for a hands-on, people-focused leader who thrives in a custom, high-mix, low-volume manufacturing environment and enjoys being close to the operation and the teams who make it happen. Reporting to the General Manager, you’ll lead plant performance across safety, quality, service, cost, people, technology, and continuous improvement while building the capabilities and culture needed to support continued growth.

**What’s in It for You**

 

* Make an impact. Lead a complex manufacturing operation where your decisions directly influence safety, quality, customer service, cost, productivity, inventory, and overall plant performance.
* Lead and develop a talented team. Build an engaged, accountable culture while coaching leaders and developing organizational capability at all levels.
* Shape the future of the operation. Champion continuous improvement, introduce better processes and systems, and help create a more scalable, sustainable manufacturing environment.
* Work across the business. Partner with senior leadership and cross-functional teams spanning manufacturing, engineering, quality, supply chain, EHS, and IT.
* Stay close to the action. This is a visible, hands-on leadership role where you’ll be connected to the manufacturing floor, your team, and the day-to-day opportunities to make the operation better.

**What You’ll Do**

 

* Provide overall leadership for plant operations, delivering results across safety, quality, service, cost, inventory, productivity, and organizational capability.
* Lead, coach, mentor, and develop plant leaders and employees, establishing clear expectations, strengthening accountability, and creating a positive, high-performing work environment.
* Maintain a strong, visible presence on the manufacturing floor, building relationships with employees and staying closely connected to safety, production priorities, and operational challenges.
* Champion continuous improvement and change management, using Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, structured problem-solving, and other improvement methodologies to simplify processes, improve performance, and create sustainable results.
* Build a strong problem-solving culture that enables teams to quickly address operational challenges, identify root causes, and continuously improve.
* Oversee staffing, talent development, performance management, goal alignment, project execution, resource allocation, and plant-wide policy deployment.
* Provide leadership and oversight of the site IT function, including the IT Manager and supporting team, ensuring ERP systems, reporting capabilities, and manufacturing technology effectively support plant operations and business needs.
* Partner across production, engineering, quality, supply chain/planning, EHS, and IT to align resources, systems, and priorities around plant and business objectives.
* Own plant financial performance by developing and managing budgets, maintaining appropriate financial controls, participating in operational and financial reviews, and taking corrective action when necessary.
* Partner with senior leadership to plan and implement new products, services, manufacturing capabilities, and the supporting processes needed for successful execution.
* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, company policies, safety programs, and business ethics standards while fostering a culture of safety and respect for people.

**What Will Make You Successful**

 

* Hands-on manufacturing leadership with the ability to balance strategic business priorities with a strong presence on the plant floor.
* Proven people leadership, including building, coaching, and developing strong teams, establishing accountability, and creating a high-performance culture.
* Strong understanding of custom, make-to-order or high-mix, low-volume manufacturing, where priorities, materials, schedules, and customer requirements can change quickly.
* Demonstrated ability to lead change, challenge the status quo, build buy-in, implement new processes and systems, and sustain improvements over time.
* Strong understanding of ERP systems and manufacturing technology, with the ability to leverage systems, reporting, and data to improve planning, visibility, decision-making, and execution.
* Solid knowledge of supply chain, materials planning, inventory, and production, particularly within a custom manufacturing environment.
* Strong cross-functional leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence across organizational lines while remaining willing to roll up your sleeves and solve problems alongside the team

**Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor’s degree in a business or technical discipline, with engineering preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive production/manufacturing management experience, including significant leadership responsibility within a manufacturing operation.
* Demonstrated business leadership with the ability to understand and drive P&L and operational performance.
* Proven success building and leading cross-functional manufacturing teams.
* Strong knowledge of continuous improvement tools and methodologies, including Lean Manufacturing and Kaizen.
* Strong business acumen with excellent communication, presentation, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
* Demonstrated ability to work across organizational boundaries and translate business priorities into operational execution.

**What Will Make You Stand Out**

 

* Experience leading a custom, build-to-order, high-mix/low-volume manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated success leading significant operational change, process improvement, or manufacturing transformation initiatives.
* Strong experience with ERP systems, manufacturing technology, and data/reporting, including the ability to use technology to improve operational visibility and execution.
* Strong working knowledge of supply chain, inventory management, materials planning, and just-in-time concepts.
* Experience working successfully within a matrixed organization.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma certification.
* Bilingual Spanish/English capabilities

 

**Why should you join Arktura LLC, a subsidiary of Armstrong World Industries?**

**About Arktura LLC**

At Arktura, we make design happen. Creativity, expert knowledge and cutting-edge technology shape everything we do whether it's exploring form and function in our standard architectural product, adapting our pre-configured architectural systems to meet project needs, or partnering with clients through our Solutions Studio. Our multidisciplinary team brings together architects, designers, programmers, engineers and artists with a deep understanding of the creative process. We use our collective ingenuity to bridge the gaps between design intent and manufacturing capabilities, creating proprietary software and machinery to meet evolving demands.

Please visit our website at www.arktura.com to learn more about us.

**About Armstrong World Industries, Inc.**

Armstrong World Industries (AWI) is a leader in the design and manufacture of innovative commercial and residential ceiling, wall and suspension system solutions in the Americas. With approximately $1.3B in revenue, AWI has about 3,600 employees and a manufacturing network of twenty-one facilities in North America.

At home, at work, in healthcare facilities, classrooms, stores, or restaurants, we offer interior solutions that help to enhance comfort, save time, improve building efficiency and overall performance, and create beautiful spaces.

For more than 160 years, we have built our business on trust and integrity. It set us apart then, and it sets us apart now, along with our ability to collaborate with and innovate for the people we're here to serve - our customers, our shareholders, our communities and our employees.

We are committed to developing new and sustainable ceiling solutions, with design and performance possibilities that make a positive difference in spaces where we live, work, learn, heal and play. It's an exciting, rewarding business to be in, and we're committed to continue to grow and prosper for the benefit of all of our stakeholders. We hope you join us.

**Our Sustainability Ambition**

"Bringing our Purpose to Life" - lead a transformation in the design and building of spaces fit for today and tomorrow. We are committed to:

Engaging a diverse, purpose-driven workforce; Transforming buildings from structures that shelter into structures that serve and preserve the health and well-being of people and planet; Pursuing sustainable, innovative solutions for spaces where we live, work, learn heal and play; Being a catalyst for change with all of our stakeholders; and Making a positive difference in the environments and communities we impact.

**About the location (Carson, CA)**

Carson is a city in the South Bay and the Harbor regions of Los Angeles County, California, located 13 miles south of downtown Los Angeles. existing_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing Engineering, Imaging
existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE JOB** 
 
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering, your role encompasses the strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering and systems to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production in Waltham, MA. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality products to our customers. Your leadership will also guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing's capacity commitments while driving advancements in digital tools and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable approach to solving complex manufacturing challenges in a highly dynamic environment. 
 
**WHAT YOU'LL DO:**

* **Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team:** Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers and technical staff. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
* **Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology:** Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril Imaging's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
* **Lead New Product Introduction (NPI):** Partner with R&D and product development teams to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM) and Design for Assembly (DfA) principles early in the development cycle to de-risk production scaling.
* **Scale Production Capability:** Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
* **Drive Continuous Improvement & Complexity Reduction:** Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive commonality optimization, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization to simplify production at scale.
* **Resource & Budget Management:** Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.

#### **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.
* Demonstrated experience owning manufacturing value chains for complex electro-mechanical or imaging hardware — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.
* Strong background in make-vs-buy analysis, contract manufacturer management, and supplier development for precision hardware.
* Experience managing NPI and scaling production in high-growth environments with condensed timelines.
* Familiarity with optical system integration and test, precision assembly, or imaging hardware manufacturing.
* Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.
* Familiarity with quality systems (ISO 9001/AS9100) and PLM, MES, and ERP systems.
* Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware (assembly, soldering, machining, fabrication, etc.).
* Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

 

### **Benefits**

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you're supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. *For more information,* *Explore Our Benefits**.*

 

### **Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

* **No Financial Requests:** Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* **Please always verify communications:**
 + Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will *only* come from an @anduril.com address.
 + Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
* **Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:** If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* **What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:** Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

### **Data Privacy**

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

 

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. We are seeking an experienced **NPI Director North America - Solutions** to provide regional leadership for New Product Introduction across North America, covering the relevant manufacturing sites and Design Center capabilities. The role translates business and customer priorities into a coherent NPI strategy, governance model and project portfolio, ensuring that new products move from concept to stable commercialization with the required quality, cost, timing, compliance and manufacturability. The role aligns Commercial, Global Design Center, NPI, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement and Manufacturing and develops the capabilities required for consistent execution across sites..

**Key Responsibilities:**

**NPI strategy and governance**

* Translate the global NPI strategy into the North American operating model, stage-gate governance, priorities and decision routines, aligned with the Global Accounts and Global Design Center Director.
* Own the North American NPI portfolio and facilitate prioritization, resource allocation, escalation and trade-off decisions across customer programs and manufacturing sites in the region.
* Implement and continuously improve common global standards, templates, performance measures and management routines for product development, prototyping, design transfer, validation and industrialization.
* Ensure early NPI and Design Center involvement in strategic customer opportunities and new product concepts.

**Portfolio delivery and industrialization**

* Oversee major and complex NPI programs from concept through commercialization and stable production handover.
* Ensure projects have clear business cases, requirements, milestones, risks, accountabilities and readiness criteria.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, cost engineering, value engineering and manufacturability reviews before production commitment.
* Ensure product concepts are technically feasible, compliant, financially viable and transferable across the relevant North American manufacturing network, while ensuring effective transfer to or from other regions when required.
* Lead executive-level reviews of portfolio status, critical risks, capacity constraints and recovery plans.

**Cross-functional and customer leadership**

* Act as the senior NPI interface for strategic customer programs and align customer expectations with operational capabilities.
* Build strong collaboration across Commercial, Business Development, Design, Engineering, R&D, Quality, Procurement, Supply Chain and Manufacturing.
* Coordinate North American and global resources to resolve cross-functional issues and accelerate decision making.
* Promote disciplined change control and transparent communication throughout the development and industrialization process.

**Capability and team leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the North American NPI organization with teams in Seattle, Dallas and East-Longmeadow, including regional managers, project leaders and specialist resources.
* Build project management, product industrialization, risk management and technical problem-solving capabilities.
* Contribute to global communities of practice and promote best-practice sharing across North American sites and with other regions.
* Foster a culture of customer focus, innovation, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications and Requirements:**

* Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, product development, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Significant leadership experience in NPI, product development, engineering, industrialization or complex program management within a multi-site manufacturing environment.
* Demonstrated experience establishing governance, managing portfolios and leading major cross-functional product introductions.
* Strong commercial awareness and ability to balance customer value, technical feasibility, operational risk and financial performance.
* Excellent communication, influencing and decision-making skills in an international and multicultural environment.
* Fluent professional English; additional languages are an advantage. Ability to travel across North America and internationally when required.

* Climate controlled facility
